title: forge ml discover document (forge.dev/ml-discover/v1)
description: What a cluster runs for ML, the recommendations, and the proposed ml.k: the output of `forge ml discover --json`. Generated from the Go type forge encodes it with.

context.description: Context is the kube context the snapshot was read through.

server_version.description: ServerVersion is the API server's gitVersion.

collected_at.description: CollectedAt is when the snapshot was read.

cloud.description: Cloud is where the nodes run, from their labels and provider IDs: one of CloudGKE, CloudEKS, CloudAKS, CloudOther.

provider.description: Provider is the infrastructure the nodes' providerIDs name, managed service or not: one of ProviderGCP, ProviderAWS, ProviderAzure, or empty. A self-managed cluster on EC2 is Cloud "other", Provider "aws".

accelerators.description: Accelerators groups the accelerator nodes by (vendor, resource, product, pool).

machines.description: Machines is one row per node that has accelerator capacity.

components.description: Components is every ML-relevant component found, in a stable order (category, then kind, then namespace).

coverage.description: Coverage is one row per observability signal an ML cluster should have (see the Signal constants): whether it is collected, by what, how that was determined, and what is missing. It is what the console's coverage-gap view reads. Every signal in Signals() has a row, so an absent signal is a row with StatusMissing, never an absent row.

warnings.description: Warnings says what discovery could not see or apply: a refused list, a CRD whose controller is missing, an env whose decisions did not render. An absence is never overstated.

findings.description: Findings are the recommendations, worst first; a finding an env's forge.RecommendationDecision dismisses is still listed, marked, last.

proposal.description: Proposal is the env's ml.k as discovery proposes it.

snapshot.description: Snapshot is where this run's read was saved (.forge/state/ml-inventory-<context>.json inside a project, or --save-snapshot), when it was.

AcceleratorGroup.description: AcceleratorGroup is a set of nodes carrying the same accelerator.

vendor.description: Vendor is one of the Vendor constants.

resource.description: Resource is the extended resource the devices are requested by (nvidia.com/gpu, amd.com/gpu, google.com/tpu, aws.amazon.com/neuroncore, habana.ai/gaudi).

product.description: Product is the device model when a label names it (NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3, from GFD's nvidia.com/gpu.product or cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator).

pool.description: Pool is the node pool when a label names it (GKE, EKS, AKS, Karpenter).

nodes.description: Nodes is how many nodes are in the group.

capacity.description: Capacity and Allocatable sum the nodes' status for Resource; Allocatable below Capacity means the device plugin marked devices unhealthy.

allocated.description: Allocated sums the Resource limits of the running and pending pods bound to these nodes.

sharing.description: Sharing is how devices are shared when a label says so: "mig", "time-slicing", "mps", or empty.

driver_versions.description: DriverVersions lists the distinct driver versions the nodes' labels report (GFD nvidia.com/cuda.driver.*), sorted.

detected_by.description: DetectedBy says how the vendor was recognised: "extended-resource" or "label" (a label with no capacity yet: the device plugin is missing or not ready).

Component.description: Component is one ML-relevant component discovery found.

kind.description: Kind is the stable component id, the same vocabulary as forge.Adopt.kind / forge.Install.kind (see Kinds).

category.description: Category is one of the Category constants.

vendor.description: Vendor is set for vendor-specific components.

version.description: Version is the image tag (or chart label) of the matched workload.

namespace.description: Namespace and Workload locate the matched object (DaemonSet/nvidia-dcgm-exporter).

via.description: Via names what manages it when that is not the component itself: "gpu-operator" (a DCGM exporter the ClusterPolicy deploys) or "gke-managed" (gke-managed-system).

selector.description: Selector is the matched workload's pod selector, what forge.Adopt scrapes by.

metrics_port.description: MetricsPort is the container port the exporter serves metrics on.

pods.description: Pods counts the component's running pods (a DaemonSet's ready pods).

resources.description: Resources counts the custom objects of its CRDs (ClusterQueues, InferenceServices).

matched_by.description: MatchedBy lists the signatures that matched, as "crd:<name>", "image:<pattern>", "label:<key>", "capacity:<resource>", "clusterpolicy:<field>", "group:<api group>".

chart_version.description: ChartVersion is the version in the workload's helm.sh/chart label, when a helm chart installed it.

config.description: Config is what discovery learned of the component's configuration (the DCGM fields it exports, NPD's monitors and conditions, a collector's receivers), nil when it learned nothing.

ComponentConfig.description: ComponentConfig is what discovery read of one component's configuration. Each list is sorted; a field a component does not have stays empty.

determined_by.description: DeterminedBy is one of the DeterminedBy constants.

source.description: Source names where it was read ("ConfigMap/gpu-operator/metrics-config key dcgm-metrics.csv", "args", "probe :9400/metrics").

fields.description: Fields are exported metric families (DCGM field names, or the probe's metric names).

monitors.description: Monitors are NPD monitor configs (kernel-monitor, docker-monitor, custom-plugin-monitor names) or equivalent.

conditions.description: Conditions are the node condition types the component sets; Reasons the problem reasons its rules report (NPD's rules).

receivers.description: Receivers, Processors, Exporters and Pipelines describe a telemetry collector's configuration (otlp, kubeletstats, k8s_events, …; pipelines as "traces", "metrics", "logs", "profiles").

settings.description: Settings are other scalar facts worth showing, as key=value ("kubernetes-attribution=true", "interval=30000ms", "tracing.endpoint=set", "sampling-rate=10000").

Dismissal.description: Dismissal is the decision that dismissed a finding.

Finding.description: Finding is one recommendation: a rule that matched, with its evidence and the adopt-first fix.

id.description: ID is the rule's stable id (accel-telemetry-missing).

severity.description: Severity is one of the Severity constants.

confidence.description: Confidence is one of the Confidence constants.

title.description: Title is the one-line finding ("3 nodes with nvidia.com/gpu have no utilisation source").

vendor.description: Vendor and Cloud scope the finding when it is vendor- or cloud-specific.

evidence.description: Evidence lists the facts the rule matched on, one per line, naming objects as kind/namespace/name.

fix.description: Fix is what to do about it.

dismissed.description: Dismissed is set when a forge.RecommendationDecision in the env dismisses this id and has not expired. A dismissed finding is still reported, marked, and sorted last.

signals.description: Signals are the coverage signals (mldiscover.Signal*) this finding is about; LinkCoverage reads them.

kind.description: Kind is FixKCL, FixCommand or FixManual.

summary.description: Summary is the fix in one sentence.

kcl_diff.description: KCLDiff is a unified diff against the env's ml.k as Propose writes it (`--- a/ml.k` / `+++ b/ml.k`), for FixKCL.

command.description: Command is the exact command, for FixCommand.

docs.description: Docs is a URL to the upstream documentation of the fix.

path.description: Path is where the ml.k goes (--out, else deploy/kcl/<env>/ml.k); empty when neither --env nor --out placed it.

written.description: Written is true when --write wrote it this run. False with --write means the file already held exactly this.

exists.description: Exists is true when a file was already at Path.

ml_k.description: MLK is the proposed file, valid KCL that `import forge` resolves; empty when there is nothing to propose.

diff.description: Diff is the unified diff from the file at Path to MLK, when one existed and differs.

Machine.description: Machine is one node with accelerator capacity, or with accelerator labels and no capacity yet (its group's DetectedBy is "label").

ready.description: Ready is the node's Ready condition.

spot.description: Spot is true when a cloud spot/preemptible label is set.

conditions.description: Conditions lists every condition that is not the healthy value for its type (Ready=False, MemoryPressure=True, an NPD condition that is True).

sharing.description: Sharing is the node's device sharing (see AcceleratorGroup.Sharing).

driver_version.description: DriverVersion is the driver version the node's labels report.

SignalCoverage.description: SignalCoverage is one signal's coverage row.

signal.description: Signal is one of the Signal constants.

status.description: Status is one of the Coverage constants.

determined_by.description: DeterminedBy is one of the DeterminedBy constants.

sources.description: Sources are the components that provide it, as kind/namespace/workload.

expected.description: Expected and Present are the parts of the signal (metric families, receivers, condition types) discovery looked for and found; Missing is Expected minus Present. Empty when the signal has no parts.

nodes_covered.description: NodesCovered / NodesTotal count the nodes a node-scoped signal applies to (accelerator nodes for accelerator signals) and those it reaches.

versions.description: Versions are the source versions found ("dcgm-exporter 3.3.9-3.6.1").

note.description: Note says, in one sentence, why the status is what it is when that is not obvious (an unreadable kubelet config on a managed cluster).

findings.description: Findings lists the ids of the findings this gap raised (mlrecs fills it; mldiscover leaves it empty).
